expectations.text: Runs an explicit gate on whether gRPC belongs at the public edge before designing any proto or service layout
expectations.evidence: "Section 1 comes before any proto layout because it changes the design"; "## 1. Gate verdict: gRPC inside, JSON outside"

expectations.text: States that REST still carries the large majority of public APIs (roughly 83% in recent tracked counts) and that dual-stack - gRPC internally, REST or transcoded JSON externally - is the practitioner default rather than either/or
expectations.evidence: No 83% figure or REST-share statistic appears; only Square/Dropbox/Cloudflare examples.

expectations.text: Names that browsers structurally cannot speak gRPC's raw HTTP/2 framing, making a proxy layer mandatory given the React dashboards described
expectations.evidence: "Browsers can't speak gRPC's HTTP/2 framing, and your merchant dashboards call you directly."

expectations.text: Names Protobuf's binary encoding as a concrete debuggability cost for external consumers: nothing readable in a network tab, inspection needs grpcurl-class tooling partners rarely have installed
expectations.evidence: No mention of unreadable network tab or grpcurl-class tooling.

expectations.text: Names that every external caller pays the protoc/stub-regeneration cost that an internal fleet amortizes
expectations.evidence: Only says "Your 200 outside engineers have never met your protos"; no stub/protoc cost.

expectations.text: Notes that gRPC at the edge limits the ability to augment or remediate API behavior in proxies and API-management tooling
expectations.evidence: Not mentioned.

expectations.text: Checks the three genuine triggers that would justify public gRPC anyway - confirmed SDK-mediated or proto-fluent consumers, genuinely streaming-shaped workload, measured performance bottleneck consumers can absorb tooling cost for
expectations.evidence: A2 on SDK-mediated audience, A4 on streaming, and the "measured bottleneck" performance trigger are each addressed.

expectations.text: Concludes that 'we already run gRPC internally' and 'it's faster' are not among the qualifying triggers
expectations.evidence: "The other two stated reasons don't change that"; "That is a fact about your inside."

expectations.text: Identifies the 200 mixed-shop partner engineers as not a confirmed SDK-mediated audience, so Temporal's control-plane precedent does not transfer here
expectations.evidence: "Temporal's public gRPC works because its audience is control-plane engineers... A broad partner platform for payments is the opposite audience."

expectations.text: Makes the audience-reach argument explicitly: limiting to gRPC-only risks missing developers not equipped or experienced enough to consume gRPC services
expectations.evidence: No explicit argument that gRPC-only would miss developers not equipped to consume gRPC.

expectations.text: Recommends gRPC inside with JSON outside rather than raw public gRPC as the only surface
expectations.evidence: "Gate verdict: gRPC inside, JSON outside".

expectations.text: States that the gate's verdict determines which transcoding/gateway options are even in play for the next design step
expectations.evidence: Gate rules out raw gRPC, but never says the verdict determines which gateway options are in play for the next step.
